newsitem.title: MEXICO: Rules for Mexico farm futures market said due soon.
newsitem.headline: Rules for Mexico farm futures market said due soon.

text.p: Rules will be published in September so that the Mexican Agricultural Derivatives Exchange can begin trading, Jose Portillo Gonzalez, director of consulting firm Merchants de Mexico, said Monday.

"The circular will be out by the end of September...with basic working regulations issued by Banco de Mexico in accordance with the Finance Ministry and the National Banking and Securities Commission, which will provide a regulatory framework for starting up the Agricultural Derivatives Exchange," Portillo said in an interview with Reuters.

Portillo heads the consulting firm Merchants de Mexico, which has led the project to develop an agricultural-industrial derivatives market under the auspices of the Futures and Options Exchange in Mexico City.

Merchants de Mexico conducted a 1993 survey in which almost 300 medium and large investors said they were prepared to trade on an agricultural futures market. Some industrialists also expressed an interest in powdered milk, coffee and cotton contracts.
"The potential is enormous," Portillo said. "In grains we consume...between 20 million and 23 million tonnes a year, and it gets bigger with meat or poultry contracts."
